messages:
Sam Chen: Pushed a PRD draft for the embeddings + rerank launch to the docs folder. Looking for quick triage on acceptance criteria and any immediate red lines from infra/customer side. link: https://redwood.internal/prd/embeds-rerank-draft :eyes:
Lina Patel: scanning now. main customer ask again is ability to change dims without breaking rerank, right?
Sam Chen: yep. two customer scenarios: 1) they want larger dims for higher recall (1536 -> 2048), 2) some legacy clients will still send 1536 vectors. We need compatibility story and test gating.
Devon Ruiz: two options: a) support dual-dim endpoints with on-serve up/down-projection, b) force migration with clear mapping and SDK helpers. Both have cost/perf tradeoffs.
Matt O'Connor: +1 on SDK helpers. Option a) adds runtime cost and complicates batching. How big is the expected traffic mix? customer A said 30% legacy, rest new.
Anya Singh: we should quantify acceptable model-quality drop. PRD mentions "<5% rerank NDCG" as gate. Is that still what we want?
Sam Chen: proposal: absolute NDCG drop <= 0.02 or relative <= 5% across core query sets. Also require no >1% regression in top-1 accuracy for critical intents.
Lina Patel: also add latency SLOs: p95 token latency for reranker end-to-end must not increase >15ms after any runtime conversion.
Devon Ruiz: batch semantics edgecase: mixing dims in the same batch -> if we do on-the-fly projection, we need deterministic ordering (no shuffling) and per-request metadata. That breaks some batching optimizations. Could we instead batch by shape prior to kernel selection?
Matt O'Connor: we already partition requests by seq_len in runtime; adding dim partitioning is similar. But if customers send mixed dims randomly, it will fragment batches and hurt throughput. Need a cost model in PRD.
Anya Singh: QA: what about normalization differences? Some customers pre-normalize embeddings (L2) and some expect server-side normalization. If we do projection, order matters (normalize then project or project then normalize) - can change similarity ordering.
Sam Chen: good point. PRD currently defaults to: 1) accept raw vectors, 2) if shape mismatch, apply projection matrix, 3) normalize final vector server-side. But we should list both orders as edge cases and include test cases.
Lina Patel: can we add a config flag per-tenant: normalize_before_projection: true/false? That gives customers control. But complicates acceptance.
Devon Ruiz: yes, and document recommended default = normalize_before_projection=true for cosine similarity consistency. Add a note about numerical stability when projecting half-precision vectors.
Matt O'Connor: also a runtime concern: KV cache and batching for rerank pipelines — we shouldn't change how cache keys are computed. If projection is lossy, cached embeddings may not match new model outputs. PRD should require cache invalidation plan.
Anya Singh: acceptance criteria checklist idea: 
- migration plan with SDK helpers and server-side projection documented
- test harness with 3 customer datasets (legacy-heavy, balanced, new-only)
- automated NDCG/regression tests with thresholds
- latency/throughput cost model + SLO calcs
- normalization order specified + per-tenant flag
- clear cache invalidation and rollout playbook
Sam Chen: adding rollout playbook to PRD: canary by tenant, shadow mode for 48h, automated rollback if NDCG drops beyond threshold or latency increases >20%
Lina Patel: suggest adding a metric: "mixing penalty" = throughput loss when batches are split by dim; simulate at 10%, 30%, 50% legacy mix. Add to Optimize team action items.
Devon Ruiz: infra-bot: Could you run a quick simulation on the current cluster with synthetic mix 30% 1536 + 70% 2048 and estimate throughput hit?
infra-bot: Sure — submitted job 4421. Estimated throughput drop ~18% for naive batching; with shape-aware partitioning drop ~7%. Will post full numbers shortly.
Matt O'Connor: perfect — toss those numbers into the PRD under "cost impact".
Anya Singh: QA: need explicit unit tests for these edgecases: 
- client sends 1536 then 2048 in same request array (should 400)
- client sends unnormalized vs normalized vectors (server must behave consistently)
- quantized payloads (fp16) cause tiny reorderings — tests should assert tolerances
Sam Chen: noted. Also adding a small code snippet to PRD for header-based versioning: 
```
POST /v1/embeddings
Headers: Embedding-Dim: 1536
         Embedding-Version: v2
```
Server will reject mismatched body shapes with 400 unless projection allowed.
Lina Patel: policy: default allow_projection=false, opt-in via tenant flag + feature gate. Safer for enterprise customers.
Devon Ruiz: can we provide a conversion tool in SDK that does local projection for offline migrations? That should reduce runtime burden.
Sam Chen: yes SDK helper is on the checklist. Also add a migration script template and sample projection matrix generation notes.
Anya Singh: one more edge case: reranker scoring uses dot vs cosine in different pipelines. Projection changes magnitude; we must ensure pipeline uses consistent scoring (recommend normalized + cosine).
Matt O'Connor: agreed. PRD should require explicit scoring method in endpoint metadata and fallback to cosine if unspecified.
Sam Chen: OK I'm going to update PRD with these changes. Who can review acceptance criteria + tests by EOD tomorrow?
Lina Patel: I can review acceptance criteria.
Devon Ruiz: I'll validate infra numbers and add the cost model.
Anya Singh: QA will draft the test harness and sample datasets.
Matt O'Connor: I'll check runtime changes and batch partitioning plan.
Sam Chen: thanks — tagging this for planning sync tomorrow 09:30 PT. If anyone has a hard veto on default allow_projection=false, reply now.
Lina Patel: no veto.
Devon Ruiz: no veto.
Anya Singh: no veto.
Matt O'Connor: no veto. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: job 4421 complete — detailed results uploaded to /internal/projects/embeds/throughput-sim-4421.csv
qa-bot: created ticket EMBEDS-322 for test harness work and attached initial dataset samples.
Sam Chen: excellent. I'll update the PRD and ping again when ready for final approval. :shipit:
